findings.claim: The new README section and MsgPack004 doc state that members of a referenced-assembly type are not reported in the consuming project. This matches the deliberate behaviour of metadata types not being analysed, so there is no defect.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly; the defining assembly owns validation.

findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter wraps every analyzer diagnostic and silently drops any that has no in-compilation source location. This is broader than the three crashing sites. Diagnostics raised against symbols in source but outside this compilation, or with a null location, now disappear. The drop of metadata-type diagnostics fits [L8], but [L10] warns that diagnostic changes risk wrong reports. The analyzer tests need to confirm that MsgPack003, 004 and 005 still fire for same-assembly types.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests for MsgPack003, 004, 005 and 017 (the MessagePackAnalyzer tests) to confirm each still reports for same-assembly types. A mutant that makes ReportIfLocatedInCompilation always drop should fail them.

findings.claim: The README and MsgPack004 doc additions have no ledger convention behind them, and the README section is placed under the custom-formatter mixing area. Docs for an internal crash fix are optional, but the README text promises support for generic value types and record structs that only the fixed code path provides.
